anticipated_objections.objection: The KAPPA-squared track IS the escape you asked for: it uses a dome-physics-derived coupling constant (κ = 1.677 nT/µGal) rather than the generic tan-FSF, it produces a Chapman-distinct magnitude, and it lives in monitor.py — a production-facing dome file in the live-power dashboard pipeline. Sub-point 4 still calls it not-the-escape; the dome defender will press the point.
anticipated_objections.response: Two replies stack. First, the KAPPA-squared track produces −28.9 nT but the predictions page publishes −21.7 nT for the same station; the codified pass-band tests the W004 path, not the KAPPA-squared path. The dome can only claim KAPPA-squared as the dome-distinctive escape if it also concedes that the published −21.7 nT is the wrong prediction by ~33% — which would falsify the existing pass-band on its own terms. Second, §6.14 already establishes that the KAPPA-squared/W004 mismatch is an internal-heterogeneity audit issue (different formulas on different dome surfaces), not a coherent two-track theory where one track is the production prediction and the other is the dome-distinctive escape. The sub-point now points to §6.14 explicitly so the reader can follow that audit without a §6.14 detour.

anticipated_objections.objection: By dropping "monitor.py" from the not-published list, you weaken the original sub-point’s sweep. A reader will ask: "so where IS the escape not published, exactly?" The answer is now narrower (predictions.html, scripts/fsf_derivation.py only) and a sceptical reader will notice the narrowing.
anticipated_objections.response: The narrowing is correct and necessary — the original sweep was wrong. monitor.py does carry a non-Chapman derivation (the KAPPA-squared track); claiming it does not is a strawman that loses the argument as soon as a dome defender opens monitor.py. The narrowed list reflects what is actually true: the escape — a per-station FSF derived from dome physics that produces Chapman-distinct magnitudes — is not in the production-facing prediction-publication path (predictions.html or scripts/fsf_derivation.py). monitor.py has a candidate, but it disagrees with the published number, so it cannot simultaneously be the production prediction AND the distinctive escape. The narrowed claim is harder to challenge than the wider claim was.

anticipated_objections.objection: The new parenthetical adds ~50 words and risks burying the sub-point’s closing punch ("Until it is, the pass-band tests a magnitude both models compute the same way."). Style — keep the closer rhetorically clean.
anticipated_objections.response: The closer remains the last sentence; the parenthetical sits between the escape-naming sentence and the closer, which is the natural objection-and-response slot. The alternative — relegating the KAPPA-squared acknowledgement to a footnote or §6.14 only — was tried implicitly by EXP-556 and is what produced hole 1. Putting the pre-emption at the point of rhetorical exposure (right where the dome defender would object) is the standard pattern this review uses for closers (see EXP-516 bracket-strawman patch, EXP-563 sphere-in-disguise pre-empt). 50 words of pre-emption at the seam buys back the closer’s integrity.

kernel_of_truth: The dome’s instinct to compute the prediction two ways — predictions.html W004 (empirical-recalibration baseline) and monitor.py KAPPA-squared (κ-derived coupling constant) — is methodologically sound. Redundant computation tracks are how engineers cross-check, and the KAPPA-squared track in monitor.py is a genuine attempt at a dome-physics-derived per-station magnitude, not just a Chapman re-skin. The κ = 1.677 nT/µGal coupling constant is not generic — it ties the magnetic perturbation to a dome-specific gravity-anomaly mechanism in a way Chapman-Sq does not. As a derivation, that IS the kind of non-Chapman escape sub-point 4 says the dome lacks.
why_it_doesnt_save_claim: But the two tracks disagree at the publication boundary. The predictions page shows −21.7 nT for Ebro on the W004 path; monitor.py computes −28.9 nT on the KAPPA-squared path. The codified magnitude pass-band — the falsifiable rule the dome puts forward — is built against the W004 published number, not the KAPPA-squared internal number. So when the dome defender invokes monitor.py to claim the escape exists, they are pointing at a number the dome itself does not publish as its production prediction. The dome cannot simultaneously (a) hold up the W004 −21.7 nT as the prediction the pass-band tests AND (b) invoke the KAPPA-squared −28.9 nT as the dome-distinctive derivation that makes the pass-band Chapman-discriminating. Pick one: either the production prediction is W004 (Chapman-equivalent arithmetic, the sub-point holds), or the production prediction is KAPPA-squared (and the published −21.7 nT is wrong by ~33%, falsifying the existing pass-band on the dome’s own terms before any August 2026 measurement). §6.14 already audits the heterogeneity at the internal-consistency level; §4.2.5 now makes the production-vs-internal distinction visible at the point of the non-discrimination claim.

notes: Closer style matches the standard adopted in EXP-563 (KILLSHOT-SH.c4 hole 5 sphere-in-disguise pre-empt): place the objection-and-response at the point of rhetorical exposure rather than relegating to a footnote, and preserve the original closing sentence intact. The kernel-of-truth concession (KAPPA-squared κ = 1.677 nT/µGal is a real non-Chapman coupling constant) is genuine and acknowledged in the anticipated_objections section so the reviewer sees we considered the strong form of the defender’s reply. Path B (concede internal-heterogeneity) was chosen over Path A (claim KAPPA-squared is Chapman-equivalent too) because Path A is harder to defend on first principles — κ-coupling to gravity-anomaly is structurally distinct from Sq-current geometry, and Chapman-equivalence would require a separate analytical demonstration. Path B sidesteps that demonstration by routing through the audit-level argument (the two dome surfaces disagree, so neither can simultaneously serve as the production prediction and the dome-distinctive escape).
